spec.title: codkit FEAT-002: End-to-end acceptance scenarios S01–S28 (Given/When/Then)

status.comment: standalone Given/When/Then acceptance on FEAT-001; e2e harness is PROP-013

p.SCENARIO-CONVENTIONS: `$TOOL`, `$PATCHES`, `$FORK` are three unrelated disjoint roots; the cwd is in a fourth place. A clean fork is a checkout of the upstream pin without local edits. A Then over the output is checked through the schema-2 `roots.tool|patches|fork`; the exceptions are explicit human-message checks. The codes are 0/1/2/3 from PROP-007.

p.SCENARIO-EXECUTION: The scenarios are a permanent acceptance contract and do not depend on a removed campaign or on a consumer product. A particular execution plan may group them however it likes, but it cancels no Then.

s01.title: S01 — load with a provided tree

p.S01: **Given**: `$TOOL`, a clean fork at the configured pin in `$FORK`, the FEAT-001 patch set in `$PATCHES`; both external roots are selected by env. **When**: `$TOOL/bin/codkit --json load`. **Then**: exit 0; `roots.tool.source=install`, `roots.patches={path:$PATCHES,source:env}`, `roots.fork={path:$FORK,source:env}`; generated branch is current and clean; ownDir is materialized/excluded; fork mark and `$PATCHES/.codkit/trees/<id>.json` agree.

s02.title: S02 — cloning into an empty directory (locally) and the ban in CI

p.S02: **Given**: `$FORK` does not exist; `--from <local-bare-mirror-repository>` is given. **When**: `codkit clone --from …`; then again; then `codkit clone --ci`. **Then**: the first run — exit 0, the tree is at the pin, `check-tree` passes; the repeat — exit 0, the output contains `already present`, no changes; with `--ci` — exit 2, the error `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN`.

s03.title: S03 — an idempotent repeat of load

p.S03: **Given**: the state after S01. **When**: `codkit load` again; timing and an mtime snapshot of every `src/vs/workbench/**` file before/after. **Then**: exit 0; the output contains `up to date`; not one mtime changed; the time is a fast no-op (< 5 s on the polygon).

s04.title: S04 — an edit → save → a patch with markers

p.S04: **Given**: S01; a `CK-workbench-905` marker block was added by hand in `$FORK/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.ts` through `marker new`, then one functional line. **When**: `codkit save --commit`. **Then**: exit 0; `.ckpatch` appears only under `$PATCHES/delta/patches/`; all additions marker-scoped; `$FORK` clean; patch-set commit touches only its delta; repeat save is byte/mtime no-op.

s05.title: S05 — the guard catches unextracted work

p.S05: **Given**: S01; an unmarked edit in any upstream file of the tree (one line). **When**: `codkit load`. **Then**: exit 1; the error `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with a list of one file; the hint contains `codkit save`; the tree is unchanged (the edit stays in place, the branch is not regenerated).

s06.title: S06 — an edit outside the markers is rejected by save and caught by verify/pre-commit

p.S06: **Given**: S01; a line was added to an upstream file **outside** the marker blocks. **When**: (a) `codkit save`; (b) a patch with such a line is forged by hand in `delta/patches/…` and `codkit verify` is run; (c) the same forged patch staged, and the patchset `pre-commit` git hook. **Then**: (a) exit 1, `CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER` with the file and the line, no patch written; (b) exit 1 with the same code; (c) the commit is rejected by the hook with the same code; the hook's run time on one file is fractions of a second.

s07.title: S07 — the inventory and its diff

p.S07: **Given**: the whole level-A polygon (PG-01…PG-09); the patchset branch `feature/x`, which adds one more marker intervention. **When**: `codkit inventory` on `feature/x`; `codkit inventory --diff main`. **Then**: exit 0; `.codkit/out/inventory.json` is valid against the schema of PROP-006 §3; entries hold ≥1 record of every layer (`own`, `service-override`, `entry-module`, `config-overlay`, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule`, `patch`); the metrics are filled in; the diff shows exactly one added record with the id of the new intervention; generation takes seconds.

p.S07-EVIDENCE-REQUIRED: Standalone acceptance records a fresh inventory result from the external polygon. Historical results from a removed consumer tree do not satisfy this scenario.

s08.title: S08 — an upgrade without conflicts: canonical commits, a green clean pin

p.S08: **Given**: the polygon branch `codkit/playground-134` (pin `1.134.0`) with the PG-01 intervention (the title bar; upstream did not change the file within the window) — without PG-C1 and PG-R1. **When**: `codkit cycle start 1.135.0`; then `codkit cycle continue` up to `done`; then `codkit ci --profile verify` on the result. **Then**: `start` — exit 0 or a move to advisory (exit 3 only on a non-empty advisory; for the polygon the toolchain diff is non-empty → one advisory stop is allowed, followed by `continue`); the outcome: `cycle status` — `phase: done`; the history of the cycle branch holds the canonical commits `bump pin` and `regeneration`, each with the trailer `Codkit-Cycle: 1.135.0`; `codkit.json` carries the new pin; `ci --profile verify` — exit 0 ("the delta lands on a clean pin").

s09.title: S09 — an upgrade with a rename: carrying the artifact over

p.S09: **Given**: `codkit/playground-134` with PG-R1 — the marker intervention `CK-platform-902` in `remoteAgentHostProtocolClient.ts` (upstream renamed the file to `agentHostProtocolClient.ts` between `1.134.0` and `1.135.0`, R096). **When**: `codkit cycle start 1.135.0` → `continue` up to the apply. **Then**: the rename step reports the pair with similarity ≥ 90; the patch file in patchset is renamed after the encoding of the new path, the `---`/`+++` headers name the new path; the carried-over patch is applied on trial (the outcome `clean|shifted|merged` in the report: the rename is a separate lifecycle fact, while the changes of the other R096 lines honestly give a 3-way `merged` even with our hook stable); the record of the carry-over is in `cycle/state.json.renames` and in the journal; a separate canonical `renames` commit exists.

s10.title: S10 — an upgrade with a conflict: the stop, the classification, the journal, the continuation

p.S10: **Given**: `codkit/playground-134` with PG-C1 (a hook in the constructor of `activitybarPart.ts` — upstream added a 7th DI parameter in the `1.134→1.135` window). **When**: `codkit cycle start 1.135.0`. **Then**: exit 3; the report classifies PG-C1 as `conflict`, groups by cause (the SHA of the upstream commit; the field `approx` is allowed), names the owner from the inventory; the file in the tree holds the standard conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`/`|||||||`/`>>>>>>>`). **When (continued)**: the conflict is resolved by an edit in the tree; a record is added to `cycle/log/1.135.0.jsonl`; `codkit cycle continue`. **Then**: the phase moves past `resolve`; the fix commit carries the trailer `Cause: <sha>`; an attempt to `continue` into `done` **without** the journal record — exit 1 `CK-E-LOG-INCOMPLETE`.

s11.title: S11 — upstream renamed a CSS class: the contract test is red, the message is clear

p.S11: **Given**: PG-04 (the contract test `patchset.contract.statusbar-class` over an upstream CSS class); a simulated drift: the class is renamed in the tree (the mechanics of the simulation — PROP-013 §4). **When**: a run of the contract tests (as part of `ci --profile build` or addressed directly by the runner). **Then**: the test is red; the failure text holds the id `patchset.contract.statusbar-class`, the name of the expected class and the hint "upstream contract drifted; find cause and update intervention `CK-workbench-905`" (the id of the linked intervention from the inventory).

s12.title: S12 — the R2b race: pin-guard catches a PR with an old pin

p.S12: **Given**: the patchset branch `feature/old-pin`, created before the upgrade (its `codkit.json` — pin `1.134.0`); main is already on `1.135.0`. **When**: `codkit ci --profile verify` on the merge result of the PR (the job emulated: base=main). **Then**: exit 1; a pin-guard error with the text "branch pin 1.134.0 != target branch pin 1.135.0"; the hint holds `codkit rebase-onto-pin`. **When (the cure)**: merge main + `codkit rebase-onto-pin` are run on the branch (+ the resolve, `codkit save`). **Then**: a repeated `ci --profile verify` — exit 0.

s13.title: S13 — an agent resolve: a journal without commits

p.S13: **Given**: S10 stopped at exit 3; an agent following FEAT-004 edits `$FORK` and appends its result under `$PATCHES`, without commits. **When**: inspect both Git histories, then `cycle continue`. **Then**: no agent-created commits exist; Codkit validates/extracts and creates the canonical fix commit; the agent journal attribution is preserved.

s14.title: S14 — air-gapped: a full run without the network

p.S14: **Given**: the container of PROP-011 §8, started with `--network none`; the tree is provided by a bind mount at a non-standard path; pre-filled `node_modules`/`.build` (for the build profile). **When**: `codkit ci --profile verify`; then `codkit ci --profile build`. **Then**: both — exit 0; the output holds not one attempt at a network call (the measurement method — PROP-013 §6); an unreachable pin (a variant: a tree with a truncated history) — exit 2 `CK-E-PIN-UNREACHABLE` with the exact fetch command in the hint, without an attempt at the network.

s15.title: S15 — the tree is swapped under a live cache

p.S15: **Given**: S01 cache/mark exist; a different clean checkout replaces `$FORK` at the same path. **When**: `codkit load`. **Then**: exit 0 but not `up to date`; the actual fork cannot validate the stale cache, so the patch-set is reapplied and cache/mark are rewritten.

s16.title: S16 — a double regeneration: an empty diff (three OSes)

p.S16: **Given**: the same non-empty fixture on native Linux, macOS and Windows runners. **When**: save → snapshot patch bytes/tip → restore → repeat identical edit → save. **Then**: each native run produces identical patch bytes and generated tip for the same patch-set/pin. Current Linux evidence closes only Linux; macOS/Windows remain open until actually executed.

s17.title: S17 — commits in the fork tree: save extracts them into patchset

p.S17: **Given**: the state of S01; two manual commits were made in `$FORK` on the generated branch (`--no-verify` or `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1`; campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D3/D4/D5/D6). **When**: `codkit save`; then `codkit save` again; then `codkit load`. **Then (a)**: the first — exit 0; the patch artifacts hold the lines of both commits; `refs/codkit/consumed/*` points at the former HEAD of the tree; patchset gains one new commit per tree commit — with the original subject/author/date and the trailer `Codkit-Tree-Commit` on its own sha; the tree is clean, HEAD is on the generated branch; the repeated save — "nothing to save"; `load` — "up to date". An addressed `save <path>` while commits foreign to that path exist: the branch is untouched, the commits stay in place, `info` "N tree commit(s) stay in the tree until a full save". **(b, Phase 4)**: three commits of three authors → three patchset commits with the same subject/author/date, one trailer each; the uncommitted remainder is in the patchset working tree, uncommitted; `--commit --message` adds a fourth commit (the remainder, with the given message, without a trailer); `--squash` — one commit `codkit save: squash of 3 tree commit(s)` with three trailers and the list; `git show <patchset commit>:delta/patches/…`, applied over the pin, reproduces byte for byte the file of the corresponding tree commit — the proof that the history was replayed, not only the number of commits; idempotence — through the test seam `replayCheckpoint` (a hard exit after the first state commit): the repeated save skips the replayed commit (its trailer is already in history), replays the rest, and does not duplicate; an empty state (an empty tree commit) is skipped with a visible message; a malformed `Cause:` in the message of a tree commit — blocked, exit 1, nothing written; `--squash` without tree commits — a no-op with a message. **(c, Phase 4)**: an intermediate commit with an edit outside a marker — the refusal `CK-E-HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER` with the sha/subject of that commit, patchset without new commits or artifacts, the tree untouched; the variant "the violation is hidden by a later commit" (the final state is clean) refuses with the same code — the state-by-state validation of pass 1 (P4).

s18.title: S18 — commits in the fork tree: the guard and the status

p.S18: **Given**: the state of S01; two manual commits were made in `$FORK` on the generated branch (`--no-verify` or `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1` — bypassing the hook is trivial, the guard must see the result; campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D7/D8). **When**: `codkit load`; `codkit ci --profile verify`; `codkit status`; `codkit load --fresh`. **Then**: `load` — exit 1 `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with the text "2 commit(s) in the fork tree since the last codkit apply are not in patchset yet"; HEAD, the working files and the status of the tree are untouched, both commits are ancestors of HEAD; `ci --profile verify` — the same refusal; `status` — exit 1 with `treeCommits.count = 2` and without the line `reload needed`; `--fresh` does not lift the refusal. The extraction of this work is scenario S17. A separate case `CK-E-TREE-HEAD`: the branch exists, HEAD is off it and carries foreign work — `load` and `save` refuse with the recipe for returning (`git switch <branch>`).

s19.title: S19 — half-committed work: save extracts both halves

p.S19: **Given**: the state of S01; half the work is committed in the tree (a manual commit with an edit inside a marker block), half is left uncommitted (an edit in the block of another file). **When**: `codkit save`. **Then**: exit 0; both halves reach their artifacts; the file that carried the committed line still carries it (the rebuild replays the state of the commit instead of overwriting it — the counterexample to the F9 loss path); the tree is clean; the consumed commit is reachable through `refs/codkit/consumed/*` and is named by the `Codkit-Tree-Commit` trailer of the single new patchset commit.

s20.title: S20 — the tree hook reminds about save instead of refusing

p.S20: **Given**: the state of S01 — HEAD on the generated branch, the hook installed by the latest `load` (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decision D9; the norm PROP-012 §5 `##FORK-TREE-PRECOMMIT-HOOK`). **When**: a manual `git commit` on the branch; then on a detached HEAD; then with `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1`. **Then**: all three — exit 0: the hook never rejects a commit. On the branch stderr holds "this commit is work in the fork tree" and "codkit save or codkit sync"; on a detached HEAD — "HEAD is not on codkit/applied/<tag>" and "git switch codkit/applied/<tag>" with the concrete tag of the tree; with `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1` — not one `codkit:` line. A linked worktree has no hook (the S0 level: the warning `CK-W-MARK-RO`), there the norm is held by the refusal of `load`/`save` — S18.

s21.title: S21 — the former name sync: the tombstone of the stub

p.S21: A tombstone (Phase 8 of the campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, 2026-09-06). Since Phase 1 this scenario asserted (decision D14): `codkit sync` (and `codkit --json sync`) is a stub with exit 2, stderr "codkit sync was renamed to codkit load; the name sync is reserved for the two-way save+load command", without an envelope; an alias was rejected so that scripts carrying the old meaning break loudly. Phase 8 (decision D15) executed the reservation: the name is carried by the real two-way command, and the assertion about the stub stopped being true by construction. The live contract is `CMD-SYNC-TWO-WAY` (PROP-007 §5), the acceptance scenarios are S24 and S25 below; the crash atoms are PROP-013 §5 `##SYNC-CRASH-TESTS`. The anchor itself is neither renamed nor deleted (NEVER-RENAME-OR-DELETE-A-CITED-ANCHOR): the address Phase 1–7 cited is unchanged.

s22.title: S22 — an artifact moved in patchset: save refuses before the first write, the recipe works by hand

p.S22: **Given**: the state of S01 (the mark carries the map of artifacts, Phase 7); the `.ckpatch` body of file F is edited on the patchset side (uncommitted), an uncommitted edit G is made in the tree in another file (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D16/D18; the form H1/S0.7 — formerly `CK-E-INTERNAL` AFTER the ref had been moved and F overwritten). **When**: `codkit --json save`. **Then**: exit 1, `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED`; the text holds the sha of the load, the name of artifact F and the manual recipe; **nothing is written** — artifact G is not created, HEAD and the branch of the tree are untouched, edit G stays in place (the ref did not move). **When (the recipe by hand)**: `git stash` in patchset → `codkit save` (exit 0, G extracted) → `git stash pop` → `codkit load` (exit 0). **Then**: both changes are in the tree — file F carries the text of the moved artifact, file G the edit of the tree; `codkit status` between the move and the refusal prints `loaded from patchset commit: …` and `patchset moved since load: 1 artifact(s)`. An old mark without the map (R13) in the same scenario — a warning and the old behaviour, not a refusal.

s23.title: S23 — the patchset branch is switched: the lineage; a dirty patchset at load is a warning

p.S23: **Given**: the state of S01; a branch whose tip is NOT a descendant of the load commit is created in patchset, and `git switch` onto it is run (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decision D17; hence a full `codkit save` comes before the switch, see 02-daily). **When**: `codkit --json save`. **Then**: exit 1, `CK-E-PATCHSET-MOVED`, the lineage text "the tree was loaded from patchset commit <sha>, which is not an ancestor of patchset HEAD <sha2>"; nothing is written. **When (a dirty patchset at load)**: an artifact is edited in patchset BEFORE `load`, then an edit in the tree, `codkit save`. **Then**: exit 0 with a warning about the unverifiable lineage (the value `dirty`) — the work of the tree belongs to that state, `save` goes on.

s24.title: S24 — two-way sync: non-colliding changes of both sides merge in one run

p.S24: **Given**: the state of S01 (the mark carries the map of artifacts, Phase 7); on the patchset side artifact F has moved (a line inside the marker block of the patch body, uncommitted); in the tree a commit G (inside the marker block of another file, `--no-verify`) and an uncommitted edit H (of a third file) (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, Phase 8, decisions D15/D16/D20). **When**: `codkit --json sync`. **Then**: exit 0; all three are in their places — G is replayed by a patchset commit with the original subject/author/date, the trailer `Codkit-Tree-Commit` and the trailer `Codkit-Sync-Transaction`; artifact H is created and left uncommitted; the tree carries the F line from the patchset side and the G and H lines from the tree side; `git status` of the tree is clean; the consumed ref holds the line of G; the transaction file is removed; the next `codkit load` — "up to date". Overwriting F during the rebuild is explainable (`##SYNC-TWO-PASS`): the target is `patchsetOnly`. **When (the rest)**: `codkit sync --dry-run` — exit 0, the classification is printed, nothing is written; `codkit sync` with no movement on either side — "up to date", without a transaction file; `codkit sync --discard` with commits — the commits are removed through the consumed ref, the patchset side is applied, mixed dirt — the usual refusal of the guard, `--ci` — exit 2.

s25.title: S25 — two-way sync: both sides edit F — a refusal before the first write, the recipe works by hand

p.S25: An amendment of Phase 8b (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, decisions D19/D21): before it this scenario asserted a refusal on both sides before the first write with the recipe "pick a side". The answer has changed: a both-sides conflict is a **diff3 materialization + a stop**, not a refusal (the live contract is PROP-008 `##SYNC-CONFLICT-DIFF3`, the acceptance is S26/S27 below). **Given**: the state of S01; artifact F has moved on the patchset side (uncommitted) AND file F is edited in the tree (inside the same marker block). **When**: `codkit --json sync`. **Then**: exit 1 `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED`; the text holds the target and a word about the diff3 markers, the hint holds both commands — `codkit sync --continue` and `codkit sync --abort`; the markers lie **inside** the marker block of the tree file (our line and their line are both visible); the transaction file exists and carries `conflicts[]` with the ours snapshots; patchset HEAD has not moved, the artifact is untouched, there is no consumed ref. **When**: `codkit sync --abort`. **Then**: exit 0, the tree file is byte for byte as before the run, there is no record (the deep proof is S27). The recipe "pick a side" remains the answer for an own conflict (there are no marker blocks) and for the uncommitted both-part under `--discard`.

s26.title: S26 — a both-sides conflict: diff3 in the tree file, a human resolves, sync --continue finishes

p.S26: **Given**: the state of S01 (the mark carries the map of artifacts, Phase 7); artifact F has moved in patchset (uncommitted, a line in the marker block of the patch body), file F is edited in the tree in the same block; alongside — a commit G in another file (Phase 8b, D19/D21; e2e `syncConflict.test.ts`). **When**: `codkit --json sync`. **Then**: exit 1 `CK-E-BOTH-SIDES-EDITED`; the tree file holds the diff3 markers (`<<<<<<< ours` / `||||||| base` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> theirs`) inside the `codkit:begin/end` block, both lines in place; the transaction is alive: `conflicts: [{path, materialized: sha256}]`, the ours snapshot of the conflicting file is in `rewrite`; `load` and `save` refuse with `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` (exit 1); `status` prints `sync in progress: <id>, conflicts: 1`. **When**: `codkit sync --continue` before the resolution. **Then**: exit 1, the file with the markers is named. **When (the human)**: the markers are resolved (both sides and the id of the block are kept), `codkit sync --continue`. **Then**: exit 0; artifact F carries both lines; G is replayed by a patchset commit with the transaction trailer; the tree is clean; the transaction file is removed; the next `codkit load` — "up to date". **When (the crash matrix)**: a crash on every atom (`transaction-written`, `conflict-materialized`, `state-committed`, `worktree-moved`, `mark-written`) through the seam `CODKIT_TEST_SYNC_CRASH_AT`, then `--continue` and `--abort` separately. **Then**: both roads reach a defined state; the refusing one names the file and the cause ("the markers are not resolved" / "the merge did not reach the file" — a crash between the record and the markers does not pass itself off as the human "take the tree").

s27.title: S27 — sync --abort gives everything back: the bytes by their hashes, HEAD and the branches, the commits of the run removed, a foreign commit on top — a refusal

p.S27: **Given**: the state of S26 after the materialization (Phase 8b, D21; e2e `syncConflict.test.ts`); before the run the sha256 of the bytes of the tree and of the artifact are taken — the bytes are **deliberately distinguishable** (a line with a unique suffix), so that a restore from the wrong snapshot (the base, their side, any version that is not ours) could not pass the comparison — plus HEAD/branch of the tree, patchset HEAD, `git status`. **When**: `codkit sync --abort`. **Then**: exit 0 `aborted`; the tree file is byte for byte (the comparison of the hashes before/after is **printed**); HEAD and the branch of the tree are in place; patchset HEAD has not moved; the artifact is byte for byte; `git status` equals the pre-run one; there is no transaction file. **When (after a crash of the continuation at state-committed)**: the materialization → the resolution of the markers → `sync --continue` with a crash after the first patchset commit → `codkit sync --abort`. **Then**: exit 0; the commits of the run are removed from the patchset branch (HEAD returned to the recorded one), the bytes/HEAD/branch match the same hashes, there is no record. **When (after a crash of the rebuild at mark-written)**: the same. **Then**: exit 0; the branch and HEAD of the tree are given back, the bytes match the hashes, the commits of the run are removed. **When (a foreign commit on top)**: the materialization → a commit by a human in patchset over the recorded HEAD → `codkit sync --abort`. **Then**: exit 1 `CK-E-SYNC-IN-PROGRESS`, the refusal names the sha and the subject of the foreign commit and explains the cause; nothing is touched — the foreign commit stands, the record is alive, the markers are in the file. `--abort`/`--continue` without a live record — exit 2, the honest answer "there is nothing to restore".

s28.title: S28 — gc removes what is spent and never touches transactions

p.S28: **Given** (campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE, Phase 9, decision D22; e2e `gc.test.ts`): three `save` runs with tree commits — three consumed refs; one `buildBranch` crash (a hard death of a real process in the rebuild window — the scratch `.codkit/tmp/<treeId>.index|.blob` and a tree lock with a dead pid); a `sync` crash through the seam `CODKIT_TEST_SYNC_CRASH_AT=transaction-written` — a live transaction file; a second tree, loaded and then deleted — a `.codkit/trees/` cache with a non-existent `treePath`; an unclosed `marker new` — a pending draft; a live lock of another tree whose owner is running. **When**: `codkit --json gc --dry-run`. **Then**: exit 0; the plan lists EVERY candidate with its class and action — consumed refs/tmp/the stale lock/the cache of the non-existent tree/out as remove, the transaction file, the pending draft and the lock of the living owner (with the pid and the command) as **keep**; among the removals — only the stale own lock (which the acquisition itself removes, as always). **When**: `codkit gc`. **Then**: exactly what the dry run listed is removed (the lists compared one to one, R14); the transaction and the pending draft are byte for byte (the sha256 comparison before/after is printed); the consumed refs are untouched (younger than the default window). **When**: `codkit gc --keep-consumed 1 --older-than 0`. **Then**: exactly one ref is left; the transaction is still byte for byte; only consumed refs are removed. An invalid `--keep-consumed`/`--older-than` — exit 2 before any lock.

s29.title: S29 — license check: a clean package passes, every defect of a carrier is named

p.S29: **Given** (campaign STANDARDS, PROP-014 §2–3; unit `licenseCheck.test.ts`, e2e `licenseCheck.test.ts`, the differential `licenseReference.test.ts`): the fixture is a byte-for-byte copy of the shipped package (`vibe.toml` with `license = "UPL-1.0"`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `LICENSES/UPL-1.0.txt`, `LICENSES/MIT.txt`, `REUSE.toml` with one annotation, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, three XML specs, `assets/codkit.svg`, `assets/codkit-mark.svg`, `assets/codkit.png` and `assets/codkit-128.png` with sidecars, `assets/third-party/feather/package.svg` + a sidecar). **When**: `codkit license check <dir>`. **Then**: exit 0, `11 files checked, 0 problems`, `--json` — `problems: []`, `checked` lists eleven files in lexicographic order with `carrier` (`header` for the specs, the README, the notices, `vibe.toml`, both SVGs of the mark; `sidecar` for both PNGs and the third-party icon) and `kind` (`own`/`third-party`), `licences.thirdParty = ["MIT"]`. **When (one defect per copy, the oracle `tools/license-fixtures.py`)**: (a) a spec without a header; (b) a header below the 20th non-empty line; (c) `GPL-3.0-only` on an own file; (d) `SPDX-License-Identifier: UPL`; (e) a PNG without a sidecar; (f) `data.json` without a sidecar; (g) the holder `Oleg Chiruhin` (a typo) without an annotation; (h) an orphan `ghost.txt.license`; (i) `LICENSE` with one word changed; (j) `vibe.toml` with `license = "MIT"`; (k) a superfluous `LICENSES/BSD-2-Clause.txt`; (l) a symbolic link inside the package; (m) an own copyright line without a year; (n) a third-party file without an annotation; (o) the licence of a third-party file `GPL-3.0-only` in the annotation and in the carrier; (p) the carrier says `ISC`, the annotation says `MIT`; (q) a stale `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`; (r) `LICENSES/MIT.txt` is missing. **Then**: in every case exit 1 and among the problems — the expected code with the expected path (`LICENSE-HEADER` for a–f, h, m; `LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY` for g, n, o, p, q; p.S58: **Given**: an edit of a file inside `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/agent-skills/v…/`. **When**: `codkit standards check`. **Then**: `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` with the path and the name of the package, exit 1; `standards load` refuses with the same code; deleting the directory and a repeated `load` — clean.

s59.title: S59 — load --fresh --discard discards the edits of the working tree by name

p.S59: **Given**: a tracked upstream file of the tree without marker blocks is changed (a build artifact). **When**: `codkit load --fresh`. **Then**: `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with the path. **When**: `codkit load --fresh --discard`. **Then**: the plan holds `discard <path>`, the file is returned to the pin plus the delta, own files are untouched, exit 0; `--json`: `data.discardedPaths`. **Given**: a file with a marker block is changed outside the block. **When**: `codkit load --fresh --discard`. **Then**: the refusal `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with the path and the hint about `save`, nothing is discarded. **Given**: `codkit load --discard` without `--fresh` over a dirty file. **Then**: the refusal `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` — without `--fresh` the flag touches commits only.

s60.title: S60 — an edition extended in place arrives through --upgrade

p.S60: **Given**: a product with `standards/v1.0.0` of the former bytes installed, the tool with the same edition number (the development version, `DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0`) and extended content. **When**: `codkit standards check`. **Then**: `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` with the list and the hint about `--upgrade`. **When**: `codkit standards load`. **Then**: a refusal with the same code, nothing is written. **When**: `codkit standards load --upgrade`. **Then**: the plan `replace`/`remove`, the directory equals the shipped one, the manifest block `unchanged` (the same version), `next: vibe install --offline --force`; after it `STATIC.md` holds `LAW-OWN-IS-DOCUMENTED`, and the materialized flow under `vibevm/vibedeps/…` holds `MI-OWN-README-ROUTES-TO-THE-OWNING-SPEC`.

s61.title: S61 — gen feature writes a header in the form of the product and puts the test in the directory of the feature

p.S61: **Given**: a product with `delta/own/`. **When**: `codkit gen feature acme.sample --title Sample --holder Acme --license MIT --header-style block`. **Then**: exit 0; three files under `delta/own/contrib/sample/` — `common/sample.ts`, `browser/sample.contribution.ts`, `test/browser/sample.test.ts`; each begins with a block header in the form of upstream with `Copyright (c) <year> Acme. All rights reserved.` and `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` inside the block; `--json` `data.headerStyle = "block"`, `data.files` — these three paths; the reminder names one unit `delta/own/contrib/sample`. **When**: in another product `codkit gen feature acme.sample --title Sample --header-file delta/own/HEADER.txt`, where the file is the block comment of the product with a line feed at the end. **Then**: the header of every file is byte for byte equal to that file, `data.headerStyle = "file"`. **When**: `--header-file … --holder Acme`. **Then**: exit 2, nothing is written. **When**: `--header-style block` without `--holder`/`--license`. **Then**: exit 2, nothing is written.

s62.title: S62 — status names the stranded materialization of an own extension

p.S62: **Given**: a product with a declared own extension `sample`, the tree after `codkit load` (the directory `extensions/sample/` is materialized, untracked). **When**: the declaration of `sample` is removed from `patchset.delta.json` together with `delta/own-extensions/sample/`, then `codkit load` (without `--fresh`) and `codkit status`. **Then**: `load` exits 0 and does not touch the directory (the guard exception for a stranded materialization, PROP-008 `DRIFT-GUARD-PREDICATE`; for the other commands the same directory stays what it was: `cycle start` refuses `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` with that path, the two-way `sync` — `CK-E-NEW-FILE-IN-UPSTREAM-ZONE` (the extracting half fires before the guard), while `ci` and `publish` go by a fresh pass, where the untracked is taken away by the cleanup, and do not refuse — that was so before the exception too); `status` prints `own extensions: 0 declared, 0 path(s) differ between tree and patchset, 1 stranded materialization(s)`, the line ` extensions/sample/ - codkit load --fresh removes it`, and exits 1; `--json` `data.ownExtensions.stranded = ["extensions/sample/"]`. **When**: `codkit load --fresh`. **Then**: there is no directory, `status` prints `0 stranded` and exits 0. **Given** in addition: an untracked directory `extensions/local-experiment/` without a `package.json` — **Then** it too is named stranded (the rule is about the declaration and the pin, not about the content), while an upstream directory from the pin is never counted as stranded.

s63.title: S63 - schema 1 is refused; the migrated VS Code patch set behaves as before

p.S63: **Given**: a `codkit.json` of schema 1 (no `type`, no `typeConfig`) in `$PATCHES` and a fit tree in `$FORK`. **When**: any command that needs a patch set, `codkit --json status` for instance. **Then**: exit 2, `CK-E-CONFIG` naming exactly the two fields to add - `type` and `typeConfig.ownRoot` - and nothing is read further and nothing is written (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-SCHEMA-2-REQUIRED`). **When**: the same patch set with `"type": "vscode"` and `"typeConfig": {"ownRoot": "src/vs/patchset"}` added. **Then**: `load`, `status`, `save`, `verify` and `ci --profile build` give the same results, the same artifacts and the same exit codes as before the split; `where` prints `type: vscode` and the envelope carries `codkit.type`.

s64.title: S64 - codkit types lists the official types and their capabilities

p.S64: **Given**: an installed tool, no patch set required. **When**: `codkit --json types`. **Then**: exit 0; `data.types` holds one row per registered type (`vscode`, `generic`, `theia` as they ship) with `id`, `package`, `version`, `installed` and `capabilities`; the human output is the capability matrix (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#CMD-TYPES`). The command reads no `codkit.json` and takes no lock.

s65.title: S65 - a capability the type lacks, and a type the registry does not know

p.S65: **Given**: a patch set of type `generic`. **When**: `codkit imageset gen`. **Then**: exit 2, `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` naming the type `generic` and the capability `brand-images`, before any write; the same for `gen brand`, `build up` and `runtime load`, and `verify` over an artifact of a layer the type does not provide (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`). **Given**: a `codkit.json` with `"type": "kettle"`. **When**: any command. **Then**: exit 2, `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN` naming the identifier and the package the registry expected; no command proceeds (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-UNKNOWN`).

s66.title: S66 - the generic polygon passes the cycle end to end

p.S66: **Given**: the synthetic generic polygon of FEAT-001 §6 - a fixture git upstream with no product model - and a patch set of type `generic` with `own`, `patch`, `resource-file`, `rewrite-rule` and a declared JSON `config-overlay`. **When**: `load`, an edit, `save`, `verify`, `cycle start`/`continue` onto the second fixture pin, `ci --profile verify`. **Then**: every step ends 0 (or 3 at a declared stop point of the cycle, resolved and continued), the inventory explains every generated path exactly once, and no step names a fact of another type.

s67.title: S67 - the VS Code polygon passes everything it passed before the split

p.S67: **Given**: the VS Code-shaped polygon of FEAT-001 §§1-5 on a patch set of type `vscode`. **When**: the whole scenario set S01-S62 is run over it. **Then**: every Then holds unchanged - the extraction of the type is invisible from the outside; the only new output is the type printed by `where` and carried in `codkit.type`. A red Then here is a regression of the split and not a change of contract (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-SCENARIOS`).

s68.title: S68 - the packages a patch set is delivered are its type's

p.S68: **Given**: a patch-set repository with a vibevm manifest and a `codkit.json` of type `vscode`, and no fork tree. **When**: `codkit standards load`. **Then**: exit 0; three packages are delivered - `standards`, `agent-skills` and `seams-vscode` - the manifest block carries one table per package, and the components block of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` lists all three. **Given**: the same repository at type `generic`. **When**: the same command. **Then**: exit 0 with the two universal packages only, and no `seams-vscode` directory anywhere; `standards check` calls that state clean, because a package no type named is a package this patch set was never promised (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-014#STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`). **Given**: a patch set with no `codkit.json`. **When**: `codkit standards load`. **Then**: exit 2, `CK-E-CONFIG` saying there is no project type to ask, and not a byte written.

s69.title: S69 - a product on the packages of the previous edition upgrades with no manual step

p.S69: **Given**: a patch set of type `vscode` carrying the packages as the previous codkit shipped them - a `standards` package with the seam catalogue inside it, `agent-skills`, and the runtime library under `delta/own/codkit/` - installed, materialised and passing `vibe check`. **When**: `codkit standards load --upgrade` and `codkit runtime load --upgrade`, then `vibe install --offline --assume-yes`. **Then**: both commands exit 0 with no hand editing anywhere in between: the standards package is `upgraded` and its copy of the seam catalogue is named under `remove`, `seams-vscode` is `created`, the runtime library is delivered under the identifier of the type, every transfer is named on its own line, the manifest block gains the third package, and afterwards `vibe check --quiet` reports no error, `vibe skill list` still names the four skills, and `codkit standards check` and `codkit runtime check` both say the installation is current (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-014#STD-LOAD-UPGRADE`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-015#RT-LOAD-UPGRADE`).

s70.title: S70 - the theia polygon: the tree is proved by the fingerprints of its family

p.S70: **Given**: the synthetic Theia polygon of FEAT-001 §7 and a patch set of type `theia`. **When**: `codkit --json where` and `codkit --json check-tree`. **Then**: exit 0 both times, the envelope carries `codkit.type: "theia"`, and the checks include `fingerprints`, ok. **Given**: the same tree with `packages/core/package.json` at a version `lerna.json` does not state. **When**: `codkit check-tree`. **Then**: exit 2, `CK-E-NOT-UPSTREAM` naming the file and both versions - a tree in the middle of a version bump is not a tree to work on (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-002#THEIA-TREE-FINGERPRINT`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-008#ID-CHECK-FINGERPRINTS`).

s71.title: S71 - the own package is a workspace package, and no upstream file is touched

p.S71: **Given**: the same polygon. **When**: `codkit load`. **Then**: exit 0; the whole own package - its manifest with `theiaExtensions`, its `tsconfig.json`, its `.eslintrc.js` and its sources - stands at `packages/<name>/`, and the only upstream file that changed is the target of the delta's own hook patch: own code reached the application by one line of the application's own dependency list and not by a graft (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-003#THEIA-OWN-IS-INCLUDED-BY-DEPENDENCY`). The application manifest is still upstream's, because this family has no development channel. **When**: `codkit overlay apply <application>/package.json`. **Then**: exit 0 and the manifest carries the product's `applicationName`, its `productName` and the dependency on the own package; `overlay check` says `materialized: true`; the inventory explains every generated path exactly once.

s72.title: S72 - a service override is the rebind and the dependency edge together

p.S72: **Given**: the same polygon, whose own package rebinds a service of the framework package it depends on. **When**: `codkit verify`. **Then**: exit 0. **Given**: the same patch set with that dependency removed from the manifest of the own package. **When**: `codkit verify`. **Then**: exit 1 with a finding naming the override, the package that binds the service and the load order: without the edge the collector may load the own module first and the rebind is overridden itself (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-003#THEIA-OVERRIDE-VERIFIER`).

s73.title: S73 - the layers and the verbs this family does not have

p.S73: **Given**: the same patch set with a patch whose header declares the layer `entry-module`. **When**: `codkit verify`. **Then**: exit 2, `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` naming the artifact, the layer and the type: this family includes own code by a dependency line and has no entry module to graft into (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-003#THEIA-NO-ENTRY-MODULE`). **When**: `imageset gen`, `gen brand`, `runtime load`, `runtime check`. **Then**: exit 2 each, `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` naming the missing capability, before any write. **When**: `build status --channel all`. **Then**: exit 0 over the two channels of the family, `typecheck` and `bundle` - the capability this type does declare.

s74.title: S74 - the cycle of a Theia patch set stops for the advisory of its family

p.S74: **Given**: the same polygon at the first pin, with the tree's dependency receipts in place. **When**: `codkit cycle start v1.76.0` without `--ci`. **Then**: exit 3 at the advisory stop, and the report names the readers that changed - the version of the monorepo, read from `lerna.json`, and the entry kinds a `theiaExtensions` array may declare (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-005#THEIA-ADVISORY-READERS`). **When**: `codkit cycle continue --ci` while the lint of the tree is red. **Then**: exit 3 with `stop: stabilize-red` - the gates of the upstream run over the tree the cycle built. **When**: `codkit cycle continue --ci` again, with the gates green. **Then**: exit 0, `status: completed`, and `codkit.json` carries the second pin.

s75.title: S75 - two owned directories, and the build output inside one of them

p.S75: **Given**: the Theia polygon, whose type owns two directories - the own package and the application - and whose delta carries the application's bundler entry and its notice under `delta/own-roots/application/` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#OWN-ROOTS-IN-THE-DELTA`). **When**: `codkit load`. **Then**: exit 0; both directories are materialized, and the application's `package.json` - the file the pin ships inside that directory - is still upstream's, because inside an owned directory the pin is the boundary and that file is the overlay's target. **When**: `codkit load` again, then `codkit status` and `codkit verify`. **Then**: exit 0 each, `own.changed` is zero: the files the pin ships inside an owned directory are not own code the delta lost. **When**: the own package is compiled in place - `lib/**`, `*.tsbuildinfo`, `.eslintcache` inside the owned directory - and `codkit status`, `codkit load` and `codkit save` are run over the compiled tree. **Then**: exit 0 each; the build output is not counted as changed own code, the load leaves it where the build put it, and `save` extracts the edited source and none of the output (`spec://codkit/modules/theia/PROP-004#THEIA-OWN-ROOT-CARRIES-ITS-BUILD-OUTPUT`). **When**: `codkit load --fresh`. **Then**: exit 0, the build output is gone and the own sources are still there - the fresh pass is the one run that removes what a build wrote inside an owned directory.

s76.title: S76 - a forbidden patch target the delta already carries as a resource

p.S76: **Given**: a patch set whose type forbids patching a generated file the install rewrites, and whose delta carries that same path in the resource-file layer, over a loaded tree. **When**: the tree regenerates the file - an install writes new bytes into it - and `codkit save` runs. **Then**: exit 0; the copy under `delta/resources/files/` holds the tree's bytes, no patch artifact is written for the path, the report names the target with the resource copy as its artifact and the action `updated`, and the rebuilt branch materializes the resource, so `status` counts no changed upstream file afterwards (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#SAVE-UPDATES-A-CARRIED-RESOURCE`). **When**: the tree writes back exactly the bytes the delta already carries. **Then**: exit 0 and the copy is untouched. **Given**: the same forbidden path with no entry in any layer of the delta. **When**: the tree changes it and `codkit save` runs. **Then**: exit 1, `CK-E-FORBIDDEN-TARGET` with the hint to revert the change in the tree - unchanged, because that path has no owner in the delta to receive it.

s77.title: S77 - one package run, and the tree that is a dev tree again afterwards

p.S77: **Given**: a loaded fork tree whose type answers with a package build, a packaging step of the product, two stamps and two output patterns. **When**: `codkit package`. **Then**: exit 0; the printed plan and the steps of the report are `drift guard, overlay apply, stamps, package build, package distributable, outputs, restore` in that order; the packager, which refuses when the overlay target still holds the pin's bytes, ran green - so the target was materialized before it and the stamps were in its environment, with the tree head under the name the type gave the `tree-head` stamp and the pin tag under the `pin-tag` one; the artifacts the type's `packageOutputs` name are printed; and the target is back at the pin, the dev channel is back, and `codkit status` is exit 0 (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE`).

s78.title: S78 - the two flags, and what each one leaves behind

p.S78: **Given**: the same tree. **When**: `codkit package --keep-overlay`. **Then**: exit 0, no `restore` step, nothing reported as restored, and the overlay target in the tree still carries the composition. **When**: `codkit load`. **Then**: exit 1 - an ordinary load does not withdraw packaging bytes silently. **When**: `codkit load --fresh`. **Then**: exit 0 and the target is back at the pin (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#OVERLAY-KNOWN-MATERIALIZATION`). **When**: `codkit package --skip-type-build`. **Then**: exit 0, no `package build` step, only the product's packaging command was run, and the target is restored as always.

s79.title: S79 - a packager that fails, and a tree that carries work

p.S79: **Given**: the same tree and a package build that exits non-zero. **When**: `codkit package`. **Then**: exit 1, `CK-E-PACKAGE-FAILED` naming the label, the exit code and the tail of what the command printed, with the hint repeating the command to run by hand; the second half was never started; and the overlay target this run materialized is back at the pin, so `codkit status` is exit 0 - the restore happens whatever the verdict. **Given**: the same tree with an unextracted edit of an upstream file. **When**: `codkit package`. **Then**: exit 1, `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE`, nothing materialized and the hint saying that packaging never gives up work of the tree on its own; there is no `--discard` to be given, and passing one is a usage failure, exit 2.

s80.title: S80 - the build profile raises the channels the type names, not a pair the engine remembers

p.S80: **Given**: two patch sets over the same tree and the same watch profile, whose types differ in one answer only - `build.defaultChannels`. **When**: `codkit ci --profile build` over the first, whose type names the two channels the engine used to carry as a constant. **Then**: exit 0 and the compile step names two channels, both of them the type's. **When**: the same command over the second, whose type names two other channels of the same profile. **Then**: exit 0, the compile step still names two channels, and the passes printed are those two - the channel the first type defaults to is never started (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-BUILD-CHANNELS`).

s81.title: S81 - what status advises over a file codkit itself wrote

p.S81: **Given**: a loaded fork tree over which `codkit overlay apply <target>` has run, so the one difference from the pin is the materialized overlay target. **When**: `codkit status`. **Then**: exit 1; `data.upstream.materializedOverlayTargets` names the target; the printed next step names the target, says it carries the exact overlay materialization codkit itself writes, and sends the reader to `codkit load --fresh` while naming the commands that leave the state behind - the line `run codkit save …` is not printed at all (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#STATUS-ADVICE-FOLLOWS-THE-LAYER`). **When**: an upstream file is edited beside it and `codkit status` runs again. **Then**: exit 1, the target is still classified as a materialization, and the ordinary `run codkit save` advice is back - the other recipe is right only while the materialization is the only thing there is.

s82.title: S82 - the first overlay of a patch set, written by the tool

p.S82: **Given**: a patch set whose delta has no overlay for a target the project type declares. **When**: `codkit overlay new <target> --id … --type … --owner … --reason … --contract-test …`. **Then**: exit 0; `delta/overlays/<target>.overlay.json` exists, its bytes are the canonical form the loader accepts - the schema key order, two-space indentation, one final LF - its `pin` is the `<tag>@<sha>` of `codkit.json`, its `contractTests` are the ones given, its `operations` is empty, and `codkit overlay check <target>` over it is exit 0 (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-OVERLAY-NEW`). **When**: the same command again for the same target. **Then**: exit 1, `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`, the artifact untouched. **When**: the command with a malformed id, an intervention type outside the vocabulary, an id another overlay already carries, or an owner `delta/owners.json` does not declare. **Then**: exit 1 with `CK-E-MARKER-BAD-ID`, exit 2 with `CK-E-CONFIG`, exit 1 with `CK-E-MARKER-DUP-ID` and exit 1 with `CK-E-OWNER-UNKNOWN` respectively, nothing written in any of them. **When**: the command with no `--contract-test`, or with `--layer`. **Then**: exit 2 each - the guard test is mandatory for this layer, and the artifact is the layer.
